summary: The article surveys a global trend of integrating wilderness survival training into outdoor and environmental education, profiling programs across New Zealand, Sweden, Japan, Canada, Australia, the USA, the UK, France, Brazil, Kenya and Russia. It argues these programs build teamwork, self-reliance, resilience, mental well-being and environmental stewardship, often blending traditional and Indigenous knowledge with modern techniques. The piece concludes that going beyond the classroom prepares students for an unpredictable future.
one_line: Wilderness survival and outdoor education programs worldwide teach resilience, stewardship and life skills by taking students out of classrooms into nature.
key_facts: The article opens on September 14, 2023, describing students learning firemaking in a secluded woodland as part of wilderness survival training.

Emily Torres launched the Kiwi Wilderness Academy in New Zealand on October 5, 2023, leading multi-day expeditions into the South Island; she says "the real test of education is not what you know, but how you can navigate the unknown."
Lars Svenson pioneered the Nordic Outdoor Life class in Sweden, launched in spring 2024, built on friluftsliv, which roughly translates to "open-air living".
Hiroki Takahashi's program in Japan, started September 20, 2023, uses Shinrin-yoku ('forest bathing') in cedar forests to teach conservation and survival skills.
Sarah Menard, a Métis educator, founded the Eagle Feather Wilderness School in Canada on November 1, 2023, pairing traditional Indigenous teachings with modern survival techniques.
Jack Manning inaugurated the Outback Adventure Course in Australia on September 15, 2023, emphasizing teamwork, leadership and decision-making under pressure.
Kaitlyn Hughes started the Solo Wilderness Experience in Colorado, USA, on October 10, 2023, focusing on solitude, self-reliance and self-awareness.
Benjamin Clarke, a therapist and outdoor educator in Birmingham, UK, has incorporated wilderness therapy since December 2023 in response to rising teen anxiety.
Mindful Mountains, led by French instructor Anne Dubois in the Alps, combines survival training with mindfulness and meditation.
Carlos Mendez, a Brazilian conservationist, started the Amazonian Field School on September 22, 2023, teaching students to live in harmony with the rainforest.
Bridget O'Connor's Wilderness Ethics class in Montana, starting January 10, 2024, teaches the Leave No Trace principle and frames survival and conservation as two sides of the same coin.
Samuel Ole Kinyaga, a Maasai warrior and guide in Kenya, teaches tracking and survival on the savannah, while Aleksei Petrov runs survival courses in Siberia's below-freezing conditions.
